newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals slip except for palladium.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals slip except for palladium.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures except for palladium ended weaker on Monday, depressed by easier bullion prices and the yen's moderate rebound.
Continued uncertainty over Japan-Russia contract talks helped palladium futures to end firmer, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from five yen to nine yen per gram lower, with most-active benchmark December ending down eight yen at 1,334 yen.
Most palladium futures hit their life-of-contract highs, backed by trade house buying. The benchmark December contract was up 12 yen per gram at 483 yen.
"There was large-scale physical palladium buying from Japanese end-users in recent days. We are still waiting for word from Russia," a trader at a major trading house said.

"We expect the tight situation in the Japanese market to continue for the near term. We would not rule out a possibility that spot palladium prices will rise to $128 per ounce in about one month," he said. Spot palladium was now quoted at $124.00/125.00 per ounce at 0753 GMT.
During Asian hours, spot gold firmed slightly at $344.60/90 per ounce at 0753 GMT from $344.10/60 in New York on Friday, as Japanese buying in arbitrage absorbed overseas selling.

In gold futures, private investors hunted for bargains below 1,330 yen per gram. "There was a feeling that further losses in yen-based gold futures will be limited as investors are keen to buy on dips," one trader said. For bullion, one key point is whether the initial support at $343 can be maintained, he added.
Platinum futures ranged from one yen to 10 yen per gram lower, with benchmark December ending down five at 1,353 yen.
Silver futures ranged from 0.5 yen to 1.5 yen per 10 grams weaker. Most-active benchmark December was off 1.5 yen at 191.4 yen. -- K.Takagi, Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431
